title: Chapter 3 Quiz 10
description: Repeating actions under the control of a condition, and where the condition is checked.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: In a **While** loop, when is the condition checked?
options: Only before the very first pass
Only after the very last pass
After each pass of the body
Before each pass of the body
questions.explanation: The condition is checked before the actions, so they may never run. Watch out: it is the Repeat...Until loop that checks afterwards.

questions.question: In a **Repeat...Until** loop, when is the condition checked?
options: Only before the very first pass
Only once, at the end of the program
Before each pass of the body
After each pass of the body
questions.explanation: The condition is checked after the actions, so they run at least once. Watch out: it is the While loop that checks first.

questions.question: A While loop may never execute its actions.
questions.explanation: If the condition is false at the start, the actions are skipped.

questions.question: A Repeat...Until loop always executes its actions at least once.
questions.explanation: The test comes after the first pass.

questions.question: A While loop runs **as long as** its condition is…
questions.explanation: While = as long as true. Watch out: Repeat...Until stops when the condition becomes true.

questions.question: Complete the loop that displays the numbers from 1 to 10.
questions.code:
Let i ← 1
{{1}} i <= 10 Do
    Display(i)
    i ← {{2}}
EndDo
questions.explanation: The loop runs while i <= 10. We must increase i, otherwise the loop never ends.
questions.hint: What must change on every pass?

questions.question: Complete the loop that repeats a calculation until the user types N.
questions.code:
Repeat
    Read(a, b)
    Let p ← a * b
    Display(p)
    Input(c)
{{1}} c {{2}} 'N'
questions.explanation: Repeat...Until c = 'N' stops when the user answers N.

questions.question:
What does the loop display? Count the values displayed.
```
Let i ← 1
While i < 10 Do
    Display(i)
    i ← i + 3
EndDo
```
questions.explanation: i takes 1, 4, 7. Then i = 10, and 10 < 10 is false, so the loop stops. Watch out: 10 is not displayed, because the test uses < and not <=.

questions.question:
How many numbers does this algorithm display?
```
Let i ← 10
Repeat
    Display(i)
    i ← i + 1
Until i > 5
```
questions.explanation: Repeat...Until tests after the body, so 10 is displayed once. Then i = 11 and 11 > 5 is true. Watch out: with a While loop it would display nothing.

questions.question: The right PIN is 1234. The user types 1111, 4321, 1234. Trace the loop.
questions.explanation: The counter goes up on every try, and the loop stops when the typed PIN equals the right one. Watch out: the counter counts the successful try too.

questions.question: This loop should display the numbers 1 to 5. One line makes it run for ever. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Let i ← 1
While i <= 5 Do
    Display(i)
    i ← i - 1
EndDo
questions.explanation: The counter must go up so that i <= 5 eventually becomes false. Watch out: with i ← i - 1 the test is true for ever.

questions.question: This loop should stop when n reaches 5. One line is wrong.
questions.code:
Let n ← 0
Repeat
    n ← n + 1
    Display(n)
Until n < 5
questions.explanation: Repeat...Until stops when its condition becomes true. Watch out: n < 5 is already true after the first pass, so the loop would stop at once. It must be n = 5 (or n >= 5).
